claim: Sheung Wan has a relaxed, easy-going atmosphere with historic temples, antique stores, dog-friendly cafes and fine dining, distinct from the rest of Hong Kong.
quote: Sheung Wan welcomes wanderers with an easy-going, relaxed atmosphere, making it a distinctive area compared to the rest of Hong Kong. The neighborhood offers a unique blend of historic temples, antique stores, dog-friendly cafes, and fine dining restaurants.

claim: Cat Street is officially Upper Lascar Row, a pedestrian antiques lane near Hollywood Road with stalls selling jade, Mao memorabilia, porcelain, coins and old posters.
quote: The pedestrian walkway is filled with rows of stalls selling jade jewellery, Mao memorabilia, porcelain ware, and much more.

claim: Cat Street is reached via the Island Line to Sheung Wan Station Exit A2 then a short uphill walk to Hollywood Road; vendors are largely cash-only; cafes include Halfway Coffee and Blue Supreme.
quote: Take the Island Line to Sheung Wan Station and use Exit A2... Cash is king on Cat Street, as most vendors operate on a cash-only basis

claim: Mong Kok's Ladies' Market on Tung Choi Street has 100+ stalls of affordable fashion, electronics and souvenirs, operating daily roughly 12:30pm to 11:00pm.
quote: The Ladies Market operates daily from 12:30 PM to 11:00 PM, with vendors typically setting up from 9:30 AM onward.

claim: The Goldfish Market sits on Tung Choi Street North (10am-8pm) and the Flower Market on Flower Market Road near Prince Edward MTR (7am-7pm); all the Mong Kok markets cluster within a 15-minute walk.
quote: The Goldfish Market is located on Tung Choi Street North... operating from 10:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily... The Flower Market is located on Flower Market Road, near Prince Edward MTR Station, operating from 7:00 AM - 7:00 PM daily

claim: Mong Kok Station (Tsuen Wan and Kwun Tong Lines) is the most convenient access to the markets, while Prince Edward Station is closer to the Flower Market and Bird Garden.
quote: Mong Kok Station (Tsuen Wan and Kwun Tong Lines) providing the most convenient access... Prince Edward Station offers closer access to the Bird Garden and Flower Market.

claim: Sham Shui Po, one of Hong Kong's oldest textile districts, has become one of the hippest neighbourhoods, blending street vendors and old eateries with a young creative scene.
quote: Sham Shui Po, one of the oldest districts in Hong Kong known for its textiles industry, has recently gained a newfound 'cool' status... transforming as one of the hippest neighbourhoods in the city

claim: Apliu Street Flea Market is Sham Shui Po's go-to spot for cheap electronics, second-hand gadgets, retro cameras and vinyl, while Tai Nan Street has revived as a leather/hipster street and Kung Wo is a 60-year-old tofu institution.
quote: The Apliu Street Flea Market is known as Hong Kong's go-to spot for electronics and quirky finds... Tai Nan Street has made a comeback as Leather Street and is very popular among hipsters and designers.

claim: Temple Street Night Market in Yau Ma Tei is liveliest around 8pm (roughly 6-11pm), with dai pai dong restaurants serving claypot rice, spicy crab and fresh seafood among the stalls.
quote: the market is the liveliest... The market offers traditional street-food restaurants or Dai Pai Dongs mixed among the market stalls, with snacks or full dinners of fresh fish, spicy crab, claypot rice

claim: The nearest MTR to Temple Street is Jordan Station (Exit C2, walk along Bowring Street) or Yau Ma Tei Station (Exit C), with stalls busiest from evening to midnight.
quote: The nearest MTR stations are Jordan MTR Station (300m) or Yaumatei... Take exit C2 from the Jordan MTR station and walk along Bowring St, or exit C from the Yau Ma Tei MTR station

claim: PMQ, the former Police Married Quarters, is a creative hub of two seven-storey buildings housing 100+ design studios, shops, restaurants, exhibitions and workshops, open daily 7am-11pm and a 10-minute walk from Central MTR.
quote: The PMQ complex contains two seven-story buildings housing over 100 design studios, retail spaces, and dining establishments... operates daily from 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM, with direct access from Central MTR station.

claim: Tai Kwun, the revitalised former Central Police Station and Victoria Prison compound (reopened May 2018), offers free-entry heritage exhibitions, art shows, tours, dining and shopping, open daily 10am-11pm.
quote: Tai Kwun, or the Former Central Police Station Compound includes three declared monuments... reopened to the public on 29 May 2018... Tai Kwun is open daily from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM. General entry is free.
